t: Memorandum On The Movements Of M. Fratkin, Soviet Employee April 8, 1932

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. 7592
Date 10. 4. 32.

Special Branch S.2.
April 8, 1932.

Memorandum on the movements of M. Fratkin, Soviet Employee.

The abovementioned individual returned to Shanghai
from Dairen on April 3, 1932 by the s.s. "Choshun Maru"
accompanied by his wife and son.

He is a Russian Jew, 37 years of age and a book-
keeper by profession. In this capacity he was employed
in 1927 with the local branch of State Trade Mission
(Gostorg). During December 1927 he left Shanghai for
Harbin.

According to our records as contained in File
No. I.C. 7592, Fratkin was reported to have paid during
April 1927 a sum of money to the Society of Living
Chinese Communists. Subsequent inquiries, however,
showed that this was unlikely owing to the fact that
Fratkin in his capacity as a junior clerk did not enjoy the
full confidence of the Soviet Consular Authorities.
Consequently the assignment to him of a delicate mission
of this nature was highly improbable. It is reported
that Fratkin will be attached to the local branch of
Centrosojus.

Efforts are being made to ascertain his place of
residence.

（批：R.B.S 9/4/32.）
（批：Joleg 9/4/32）

G Tchenenchansky.
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
Information.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记室
第 7592 号
日期 1932年4月10日

特别科 S.2.
1932年4月8日。

关于苏联雇员 M. Fratkin 行踪的备忘录。

上述人员于1932年4月3日由其妻儿陪同，乘“长顺丸”号（s.s. "Choshun Maru"）轮船从大连返回上海。

他是俄罗斯犹太人，现年37岁，职业为簿记员。1927年，他曾以此身份受雇于国家贸易代表团（Gostorg）驻沪办事处。1927年12月，他离开上海前往哈尔滨。

根据我处第 I.C. 7592 号卷宗内的记录，据报 Fratkin 曾于1927年4月向在沪中国共产主义者协会支付了一笔款项。然而，随后的调查显示，鉴于 Fratkin 当时仅为初级职员，并未获得苏联领事当局的充分信任，此事不太可能发生。因此，委派他执行此类敏感任务的可能性极小。据报，Fratkin 将隶属于中央消费合作总社（Centrosojus）驻沪办事处。

目前正在设法查明其居住地。

（批注：R.B.S 1932年4月9日。）
（批注：Joleg 1932年4月9日）

G Tchenenchansky.
D. S.

特别科主管警官。
情报。

May 28 27

Dear Colonel,

Further to my letter of May 27, the
two Russians named Achinine alias Oshanin and Sharoff
were released by the Chinese Military Authorities
at 3 p.m. May 27 and allowed to take their luggage
with them. Detectives of the S.M.P. were not
permitted to examine the luggage, but the Chinese
Authorities state that it contained nothing of an
incriminating nature.

Yours sincerely,

Lieut. Col. G. H. Halland, O.B.E.,
General Staff, Headquarters,
Shanghai Defence Force.

pages.en:
Copy of Police Report dated May 26, 1927.

Further to my attached report of May 26.
Elie Oshanin and Elie Charoff were taken before
Judge Y. S. Ziar in the Provisional Court at 12 Noon on May 26
when a detective attached to General Yang Hu's Headquarters
made application that the two accused men be handed over to the
Chinese Military Authorities for trial.
After hearing evidence of arrest and reading General Yang Hu's
letter to the Commissioner of Police, Judge Ziar, addressing
Detective Inspector Yorke. made the following announcement.
"I wish to draw a line in these cases. It is
"not an offence in any Country to be a Communist or entertain
"any other political views. France is a Republic yet
"Monarchists abound in that Country. You have Communists in
"England, in fact in Parliament (Here I interjected "We have one
"Communist, in Parliament, unfortunately, Sir.") A person
"can embrace any school of thought he pleases, but if his political
"views are contrary to the Government of the Country, and he
"plots against that Government, then his actions become an
"offence. Do you agree, Inspector Yorke? "Entirely, Sir."
Judge Ziar then heard the Chinese detective's
application that the accused be handed over to the Military
Authorities and again addressing D. I. Yorke said "I take it
"the Police have good grounds that the accused are, or have been
"plotting against the Nationalist Government." The reply was
"General Yang Hu and the Military Authorities must have had
"good grounds before requesting the Municipal Police to assist
"in this arrest." The Judge then said "And the Municipal
"Police must have had good grounds before assisting the
"Military Authorities." The reply was "There is every
"reason to believe the defendants are and have been acting
"in a subversive manner."
The Judge "And the Police do not oppose the application of
"the Military Authorities.".
pages.zh:
1927年5月26日警方报告副本。

继我附上的5月26日报告之后。
Elie Oshanin 和 Elie Charoff 于5月26日中午12点在临时法庭被带至法官 Y. S. Ziar 面前，当时一名隶属杨虎将军司令部的侦探提出申请，要求将这两名被告移交中国军方当局审判。
在听取逮捕证据并宣读杨虎将军致警务处处长的信函后，Ziar 法官对警司 Yorke 发表了如下声明：
“我想在这些案件中划清界限。在任何国家，成为共产党人或持有其他政治观点都不是犯罪。法国是共和国，但该国君主主义者众多。英国也有共产党人，事实上议会里就有（此处我插话：‘不幸的是，先生，我们议会里有一名共产党人。’）一个人可以信奉任何他喜欢的思想流派，但如果他的政治观点与该国政府相悖，并且他阴谋反对该政府，那么他的行为就构成犯罪。你同意吗，Yorke 警司？‘完全同意，先生。’”
随后，Ziar 法官听取了中方侦探关于将被告移交军方当局的申请，并再次对警司 D. I. Yorke 说：“我认为警方有充分理由相信被告正在或曾经阴谋反对国民政府。”回答是：“杨虎将军和军方当局在请求市政警察协助此次逮捕之前，必定有充分理由。”法官接着说：“市政警察在协助军方当局之前，也必定有充分理由。”回答是：“有充分理由相信被告正在且一直从事颠覆活动。”
法官：“警方不反对军方当局的申请。”

pages.en:
2.
Reply: "The Police Authorities fully support the application."
Judge Ziar then explained at length to the
defendants that they would be handed over to the Military
Authorities for trial and the Military Court would hear
their defence. This explanation was made in the Chinese
language direct to Oshanin who has a perfect command of that
language, both as spoken and written.
The two accused, together with their luggage
consisting of four trunks and attache cases, were escorted
to General Yang Hu's Headquarters at 1 p.m.
I respectfully suggest that Russian detectives
be sent to the Military Headquarters to assist in perusing
any documents found in the luggage of the accused.
Attached herewith is a receipt issued by the
Military Authorities for the two accused.
pages.zh:
2.
回答：“警方当局完全支持该申请。”
随后，Ziar 法官向被告详细解释，他们将被移交给军方当局审判，军事法庭将听取他们的辩护。这一解释是用中文直接向 Oshanin 作出的，他精通中文，无论是口语还是书面语。
两名被告及其行李（包括四个行李箱和公文包）于下午1时被护送至杨虎将军司令部。
我谨建议派遣俄国侦探前往军事司令部，协助查阅在被告行李中发现的任何文件。
随函附上军方当局出具的接收两名被告的收据。

pages.en:
Copy of Police Report dated May 26, 1927.

I beg to report that, on May 25, the attached
letter was received from General Yang Hu requesting the
assistance of the Municipal Police in arresting two Russian
Communists named Sharoff and Shanin who were arriving by
steamer from Hankow.
In company with P.C.S. Kedrolivansky and three detectives from
General Yang Hu's Headquarters, I attended at Hunt's Wharf at
6 a.m. May 26, and the two wanted men arrived by the s.s.
"Tuckwo" which berthed at 7 a.m. Shanin and Sharoff were
arrested and taken to Hongkew Station. An examination of their
passports showed that their names are Elie Charoff, a bank
employee and Elie Oshanin, a Secretary in the Chinese
Department of the Soviet Government. The latter's passport
is a diplomatic one. Oshanin appears on the passenger list
(attached) of the steamer as "Shanin" and he explains that the
letter "O" was omitted from his name by the servant who booked
his passage at Hankow.
These are the two men mentioned in the telegram from the Rear
Admiral of the Yangtse Fleet.
Oshanin has made repeated requests to be allowed to telephone
to the Soviet Consul-General and claims diplomatic immunity from
arrest. Both Sharoff and Oshanin have been searched but
their luggage has not yet been examined.
I respectfully ask for instructions regarding
these two suspects.
pages.zh:
1927年5月26日警方报告副本。

谨此报告，5月25日收到附函，系杨虎将军来信，请求市政警察协助逮捕两名名为 Sharoff 和 Shanin 的俄国共产党人，他们将乘轮船从汉口抵达。
5月26日上午6时，我与警员 Kedrolivansky 及三名来自杨虎将军司令部的侦探一同前往亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf），两名通缉犯乘坐于上午7时靠泊的“大沽”号（s.s. "Tuckwo"）轮船抵达。Shanin 和 Sharoff 被捕并被带往虹口捕房。检查他们的护照显示，其姓名为 Elie Charoff，银行职员，以及 Elie Oshanin，苏联政府中文部秘书。后者的护照为外交护照。Oshanin 在轮船乘客名单（见附件）上显示为“Shanin”，他解释说，这是因为在汉口为他预订舱位的侍者漏掉了他名字中的字母“O”。
这就是长江舰队少将电报中提到的那两个人。
Oshanin 多次请求允许致电苏联总领事，并声称享有逮捕豁免的外交特权。Sharoff 和 Oshanin 均已被搜身，但其行李尚未检查。
我就这两名嫌疑犯的处理请示指示。

assistance of the Municipal Police in arresting two Russian
Communists named Sheroff and Shanin who were arriving by steamer
from Hankow.

In company with P.C.S. Kedrolivansky and three detectives from
General Yang Hu's Headquarters, I attended at Hunt's Wharf at

Oshanin appears on the passenger list (attached) of the steamer

his name by the servant who booked his passage at Hankow.
These are the two men mentioned in the telegram from the Rear

由 D. I. Yorke 撰写。经 [签名] 转呈

先生：

谨此报告，5月25日收到附件中杨虎将军的来信，请求工部局警务处协助逮捕两名名为 Sheroff 和 Shanin 的俄国共产主义者，他们将乘轮船从汉口抵达。

5月26日上午6时，我与警司 Kedrolivansky 及杨虎将军总部的三名侦探一同前往汇山码头（Hunt's Wharf），两名被通缉者乘坐于上午7时靠泊的“太古”轮（s.s. "Tuckwo"）抵达。Shanin 和 Sharoff 被捕并被带往虹口捕房。检查其护照显示，他们的名字分别为 Elie Charoff（银行职员）和 Elie Oshanin（苏维埃政府华务科秘书）。后者的护照为外交护照。Oshanin 在随附的轮船乘客名单上显示为“Shanin”，他解释说，在汉口为其预订船票的仆役将其名字中的字母“O”漏掉了。
这两人即长江舰队少将电报中提及的那两人。
Oshanin 多次要求允许其致电苏联总领事，并声称享有免受逮捕的外交豁免权。Sharoff 和 Oshanin 均已被搜身，但其行李尚未检查。[手写批注：后者携带有尚未查阅的文件。其中包括一封密信。]
关于这两名嫌疑人，谨请指示。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
[签名]
D. I.

副刑事侦缉处长。

（左侧竖排批注）：
副刑事侦缉处长 你的密码 J. Smit. 如
电话所述。虹口 inward
1927年5月26日。
Sims

REPORT ON Whereabouts of Achinine otherwise called Oshanin.

Made by C. D. I. Givens Forwarded by

Sir,

With reference to attached, I beg to report that
Achinine alias Oshanin arrived here from Hankow by the s.s.
"Tuckwo" on May 26. The Municipal Police, in co-operation
with the Chinese Military Authorities, at whose request they
were acting, arrested him as soon as he landed from the ship
and took him together with another Russian named Sharoff,
arrested at the same time, to the Provisional Court which made
an order to have both prisoners handed over to the Chinese
Military Authorities.

Oshanin's description is as follows : 5'6" in
height, slim build, clean shaven, wears goggle style glasses,
brown hair, dresses poorly, speaks Chinese fluently and English
indifferently.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

[Signature: Givens]
C. D. I.

Extract from SUSPECT LIST NO. 1 dated 19.5.27(File No.I.O.7922)
------------------------------------

A-1. ACHININE (or ASHININ).

Arrived Shanghai July 1926. Secretary for
Chinese Affairs at the Soviet Consulate, Shanghai. Has
been active in attempting to undermine the anti-communist
movement initiated by Chiang Kai Shek in Shanghai. He is
reported to have distributed $11,000 in this town on the
17th and 18th April, 1927, to various Communist
Associations and to have been allotted a further $300,000
on 26th April, 1927, with which to foment a rising against
Chiang Kai Shek, but enquiries have so far failed to
confirm this information.

A-1. ACHININE（或 ASHININ）。

1926年7月抵达上海。苏联驻上海领事馆华务科秘书。一直积极试图破坏蒋介石在上海发起的反共运动。据报道，他于1927年4月17日和18日在本市向各共产主义协会分发了11,000美元，并于1927年4月26日被分配了另外300,000美元，用于煽动反对蒋介石的起义，但目前的调查未能证实这一信息。

April 20, 1927

REPORT ON Soviet agents and their Plans to create trouble in
Shanghai.

Made by C.D.I.Givens Forwarded by

Sir,
Enquiries go to show that Ashanin otherwise Achinine
is Secretary for Chinese Affairs in the Soviet Consulate
and resides with his wife in that institution. He speaks
Mandarin fluently, and has many connections among Chinese. His
photograph is attached herewith.
Fratkin, who is a Soviet Russian professing the
Jewish faith, is a book-keeper in the Gostorg (State Trade
Mission), Soviet Consular Building, and resides at No.23 North
Szechuen Road.
Koo Shi Peng (顧治本) otherwise Kou Tse Ping (顧治本)
who is an ardent Communist, is reported to be an employee of the
Chinese Post Office in Shanghai.
Madame Chelmo-Pousirevsky, No.396 Avenue Joffre, is the
mistress of General Guschin who used to be commander of the
"Red" Russian detachment in General Feng Yu Hsiang's army.
As regards the paragraphs which contain allegations
that Foreign and Chinese Communists, including the above-named,
are engaged in activities aiming at creating trouble in the
Settlement and undermining the loyalty of the Shaforce, there
seems to be no doubt that a movement of this kind has been
started. The exact plans of the subversive agents have not
been discovered, but there is reason to believe that efforts
will be made to seduce the troops from their allegiance by
propaganda and other means, and that strikes rather than armed
force will be used to create troubles of a general nature. It
is however probable that a resort may be made to assassination

由刑事侦缉督察 Givens 撰写 经 转呈

先生，
调查显示，Ashanin（又称 Achinine）是苏联领事馆的华务科秘书，与其妻子居住在该机构内。他汉语流利，在中国人中有许多关系网。其照片随附于此。
Fratkin 是一名信奉犹太教的苏维埃俄国人，是位于苏联领事馆大楼内的国家贸易代表团（Gostorg）的簿记员，居住在四川北路23号。
顾治本（Koo Shi Peng），又称顾治本（Kou Tse Ping），是一名狂热的共产主义者，据报道是上海中国邮政局的雇员。
Chelmo-Pousirevsky 夫人，住址霞飞路396号，是 Guschin 将军的情妇，后者曾任冯玉祥将军军队中“赤色”俄国分队的指挥官。
关于那些指控外国和中国共产主义者（包括上述人员）从事旨在在租界制造麻烦并破坏上海防卫部队忠诚度的活动的段落，毫无疑问，此类运动已经开始。颠覆分子的确切计划尚未被发现，但有理由相信，他们将努力通过宣传和其他手段诱使士兵背叛 allegiance，并且将使用罢工而非武装力量来制造一般性的麻烦。然而，可能会诉诸暗杀

            No confirmation has so far been obtained regarding

members of the Association of Postal workers, but inquiries are

            The report that the Young Chinese Communists have been
paid a sum of money through Fratkin is very unlikely.  Fratkin is
only a junior clerk who does not enjoy the full confidence of the
Soviet Consular Authorities.  Consequently the assignment to
him the delicate mission of giving money to Chinese Communists
is highly improbable.
            Efforts now being made to verify the information about
the receipt by the Dalbank of $150,000.00 for propaganda among
the Foreign troops would be greatly facilitated if information
could be obtained about the date of the arrival of the money,
the place from which it came, and the names of some of the
persons who have been given checks on that account.

of deserters from the Shanghai Defence Force have been discussed
in Soviet and Communist circles, but nothing is known regarding

SECRET.

INFORMATION FROM FRENCH SOURCES 16/4/27.
No. 7592
Date 20/4/27.

(a). POLITICAL AND GENERAL.

1. Bolshevik activity at Shanghai. ACHININE has ordered
KOUTSE-PING to organise a special combatant branch among
the members of the Association of Chinese postal workers.
One Branch is to be installed in the International Settlement.
Arms for the above are reported to be in the Chinese City
and KOUTSE-PING is looking for a means of transporting them
into the International Settlement.

The Society of Young Chinese Communists has received
a certain sum of money from the Russian Consulate. The sum
was handed over through the intermediary of FRATKINE.

Simultaneously with the arrival of special agents for
propaganda work among the foreign troops in Shanghai,
International Communists have allotted $ 150,000 for the
same purpose. This money was sent through the intermediary
of the DALBANQUE.

Agents of the KUOMINTUNG entrusted with propaganda
work amongst the troops have been instructed to help
deserters as far as possible, by furnishing them with money
and passports to proceed to Russia.

Madame CHELMO-POUSIREVSKY (associated with the Russian
Consulate) has moved to No. 396 Avenue Joffre.

日期：1927年4月20日。

(a). 政治与一般情况。

1. 上海的布尔什维克活动。阿希宁（ACHININE）已命令古泽平（KOUTSE-PING）在中国邮务员工会成员中组织一个特别战斗分支。其中一个分支将设立于公共租界内。据报，上述人员所需的武器位于华界，古泽平（KOUTSE-PING）正在寻找将其运入公共租界的方法。

中国青年共产党人协会已从俄国领事馆获得一笔款项。该笔款项是通过弗拉特金（FRATKINE）作为中间人移交的。

随着专门负责在上海外籍军队中进行宣传工作的特工抵达，国际共产主义者已拨出15万美元用于同一目的。这笔钱是通过达尔班克（DALBANQUE）作为中间人发送的。

受委托在军队中开展宣传工作的国民党（KUOMINTUNG）特工已接到指示，要尽可能帮助逃兵，为他们提供资金和护照以便前往俄国。

切尔莫-普西列夫斯基夫人（Madame CHELMO-POUSIREVSKY，与俄国领事馆有关联）已搬至霞飞路396号。

SECRET

Headquarters
Shanghai Defence Force

April 19th.1927.

My dear Clarke,

I enclose two copies of "information from French
sources" regarding Bolshevik activity in Shanghai. Would
you kindly give one to the Commissioner as the question of
the efficiency of our arrangements for preventing the passing
of arms into the Settlement may come up for discussion at
the conference which we are holding to-morrow at 11 A.M.

Have you any information about the individuals
named - Achinine, Fratkinе and Koutse-Ping ?

Yours sincerely,

G. M. Hallifax

Lieut-Colonel
General Staff.

W.G.Clarke Esq., M.B.E.,
Assistant Commissioner of Police (C.I.D.)
Shanghai Municipal Council

1927年4月19日。

亲爱的克拉克：

兹附上两份关于上海布尔什维克活动的“来自法方渠道的情报”。鉴于我们明天上午11时举行的会议可能会讨论防止武器流入租界的安排效率问题，恳请将其中一份交给警务总监。

SECRET
INFORMATION FROM FRENCH SOURCES. 16/4/27.
--------------------------------------------------

(a). POLITICAL AND GENERAL.

1. Bolshevik activity at Shanghai. ACHININE has ordered
KOUTSE-PING to organise a special combatant branch among
the members of the Association of Chinese postal workers.
One Branch is to be installed in the International Settlement.
Arms for the above are reported to be in the Chinese City
and KOUTSE-PING is looking for a means of transporting them
into the International Settlement.

The Society of Young Chinese Communists has received
a certain sum of money from the Russian Consulate. The sum
was handed over through the intermediary of FRATKINE.

Simultaneously with the arrival of special agents for
propaganda work among the foreign troops in Shanghai,
International Communists have allotted $ 150,000 for the
same purpose. This money was sent through the intermediary
of the DALBANQUE.

Agents of the KUOMINTUNG entrusted with propaganda
work amongst the troops have been instructed to help
deserters as far as possible, by furnishing them with money
and passports to proceed to Russia.

Madame CHELMO-POUSIREVSKY (associated with the Russian
Consulate) has moved to No. 396 Avenue Joffre.

Shanghai Municipal Police.
CENTRAL I. O. Station
January 26, 1927.
REPORT ON Mysterious Member of Staff of Soviet Consulate.
Made by P.C.C. Kedrolivansky, Forwarded by [Signature]
Sir,
I beg to attach herewith three photos of one,
Ashinin, a Soviet agent who is said to be at present
residing in the Soviet Consulate here. Ashinin is re-
garded as a mystery man by the other members of that
establishment. Although he has been about three months in
Shanghai, he seems to have no regular work. He speaks
Mandarin fluently and has several Chinese friends.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant
[Signature]
P. C. C.
D. C. I.

中央情报站
1927年1月26日。
关于苏联领事馆一名神秘职员的报告。
由警员凯德罗利万斯基（P.C.C. Kedrolivansky）撰写，由 [签名] 转呈
先生，
谨此附上阿希宁（Ashinin）的照片三张。阿希宁是一名苏联特工，据说目前居住在本地的苏联领事馆内。在该机构的其他成员眼中，阿希宁被视为一个神秘人物。尽管他已在上海待了约三个月，但似乎没有固定工作。他能说流利的官话，并有几位中国朋友。
先生，
您顺从的仆人
[签名]
警员
副督察
